questions.question: Explain two Shi'a beliefs about the Imamate.
questions.correctAnswer: 1) Shi'a Muslims believe Allah appointed twelve Imams to guide the Muslim community after Muhammad. They are divinely chosen, not elected by the people, and are descendants of Muhammad through Ali and Fatimah. 2) The Imams are infallible — they cannot make errors in interpreting the Qur'an or Islamic law. questions.question: "The Imamate is the most important Shi'a belief." Evaluate this statement.
questions.correctAnswer: The Imamate is certainly distinctive to Shi'a Islam and shapes their entire approach to authority, law and community. Without the Imamate, Shi'a Islam would lose its unique identity. However, tawhid (the oneness of God) is arguably more fundamental — it is the first root of Usul ad-Din and the foundation of all Islamic belief. The Imamate depends on tawhid but tawhid does not depend on the Imamate
